Italian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin vīvere, from Proto-Italic *gʷīwō, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷíh₃weti (“to live, be alive”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈvi.ve.re/[1]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ivere
  • Hyphenation: vì‧ve‧re

Verb

[edit]

vìvere (first-person singular present vìvo, first-person singular past historic vìssi, past participle vissùto, first-person singular future vivrò, auxiliary avére or (now less common,[2] traditional, only in some meanings) èssere)

  1. (intransitive) to live; to be alive [auxiliary avere or (traditional) essere]
  2. (intransitive) to subsist, to be [auxiliary avere or (traditional) essere]
  3. (intransitive) to live well, to experience a good life [auxiliary avere]
  4. (transitive) to live, to experience (a life of a specified type, a specified period of time, or cognate accusative)

Latin

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

vīvere

  1. present active infinitive of vīvō
    • 20 BCE – 14 BCE, Horace, Epistles 1.6.29:
      Vīs rēctē vīvere? Quis nōn?
      Do you wish to live right? Who doesn't?
    • c. 45 BCE, Cicero, Tusculan Disputations 5:
      Vīvere est cōgitāre.
      To live is to think.
  2. second-person singular present passive imperative/indicative of vīvō
